name: Do I need a permit to remove a wall for an open-concept remodel in San Diego County?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to remove a wall for an open-concept remodel in San Diego County?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, a permit question should be answered before work begins, not after demolition. San Diego County guidance says permits may be required for constructing, enlarging, altering, repairing, moving, or demolishing a structure and for regulated electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing work. Context: City rules may apply instead of County rules, and an open-concept project often combines several permit triggers. Structural wall changes may require plans, engineering information, or additional review. Key factors: jurisdiction; structural scope; utility changes; additions or altered openings. Practical guidance: Identify the property’s governing building department and have the proposed scope checked before signing off on demolition. Keep approved plans and inspection records with the home documents. Elite Remodeling & Design includes permitting coordination within its published project process.
acceptedAnswer.description: Possibly, and structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, demolition, or altered-opening work commonly requires careful permit review. San Diego County guidance requires permits for many building alterations and regulated systems. Confirm the property’s jurisdiction and scope before demolition; do not assume an interior wall is exempt.
